detail.longDescription: I am managed to run the Podman to be have a access like what Docker does by default, which involves touching the system root/daemon. What I am doing is just: # First, enable the daemon and services. sudo systemctl enable --now podman.service sudo systemctl enable --now podman.socket # Make sure it looks like this. [jimedrand@archie ~]$ sudo systemctl status podman.socket ● podman.socket - Podman API Socket Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/podman.socket; enabled; preset: disabled) Active: active (listening) since Thu 2026-08-27 05:25:23 WIB; 19min ago Invocation: 8b994fb7d3374210917b553157b6af21 Triggers: ● podman.service Docs: man:podman-system-service(1) Listen: /run/podman/podman.sock (Stream) Aug 27 05:25:23 archie systemd[1]: Listening on Podman API Socket. # Then, make the symlink for compatibility and install the Docker command emulator (install the podman-docker packages from your distro's package manager). sudo ln -s /run/podman/podman.sock /var/run/docker.sock # Lastly, test the socket after the symlink. sudo curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/_ping It gives you the same power as Docker’s default behaviour, which means Podman now has the ability to access the root/daemon. #podman #container #sysadmin #docker #devops #opensource
